title: CLAUDE.md
text: compute-intensive work C++ Rcpp bindings: netcdf_io.cpp/h — Direct NetCDF-C /O spatial/temporal subsetting, CF time parsing, scale_factor/add_offset/_FillValue handling. Supports NC_CHAR NC_STRING attributes. Reorders data pixel-major layout [pixel][time] cache-friendly per-pixel processing. Reads writes climatology, event, SST NetCDF files. climatology.cpp/h — Full ts2clm algorithm: gap filling, NA interpolation, DOY assignment (non-leap years skip DOY 60), spread DOY×year matrix, sliding-window percentile (Type-7 quantile matching R exactly), circular-padded rolling mean smoothing. std::thread parallelism pixels progress reporting. event_detect.cpp/h — Full detect_event algorithm: threshold exceedance, run-length encoding, duration filtering, gap joining, 19 event metric computations. Cold spell support (threshold inversion). Optional inline Hobday et al. (2018) category computation (Moderate IV Extreme) season assignment. std::thread parallelism pixels progress reporting. blob_label.cpp — 3D connected-component labeling (union-find, 6-connectivity, optional dateline wrap). Ported heatwaveR. blob_metrics.cpp — Per-(blob, day) spatial metric reduction. Ported heatwaveR. heatwave3_init.cpp — Rcpp exports bridging C++ R. Key exports: hw3_compute_clim, hw3_detect_events (category/hemisphere protoEvent/write_daily params), hw3_read_sst, hw3_read_event_nc, hw3_read_clim_nc, hw3_read_daily_nc, hw3_category, hw3_block_average, hw3_read_metric_summary. heatwave3_types.h — Core structs: EventResult (19 metrics + category + season), EventData (reading event NetCDF), SubsetSpec, ClimData, GridData.

Returns written paths invisibly. ts2clm3() — NetCDF → climatology NetCDF (seas + thresh per DOY per pixel) <name>_clim.nc. detect_event3() — SST + climatology → event NetCDF. clim_file defaults <name>_clim.nc. Supports category = TRUE (inline categories) hemisphere = "south"/"north". Per-day output via daily = c("none","also","") (writes <name>_events_daily.nc temp/seas/thresh/intensity/event/event_no + daily category) protoEvent = TRUE (writes <name>_protoevents.nc heatwaveR proto flags, instead event table). per-day products gridded [lon, lat, time]. hw3_export() — Read/export hub: auto-detects product (via hw3_file_meta), returns long data.frame (whole first n rows) writes flat .csv/.rds/.parquet. Returns full daily grid columns daily="also" product (lon, lat, t, temp, seas, thresh, intensity, event, event_no, category); category set event-member exceedance days NA elsewhere, ice_thresh cold-spell ice category. MHW Tracker’s load_sub_cat_clim() event-day subset subset(x, !.na(category)). block_average3() — Yearly event metric aggregation (pure C++) exceedance3() — Static threshold exceedance detect_blob3() — 3D spatially-connected blob detection event_line3() — Per-pixel time series plot NetCDF (C++ reader, ncdf4) geom_flame3() / geom_lolli3() — ggplot2 custom geoms plot_metric3() — Spatial map event metrics (C++-backed aggregation via hw3_read_metric_summary)

text: Pixel-major memory layout: SST data reordered [pixel][time] contiguous per-pixel time series access std::thread parallel loops. title: Performance benchmark: heatwave3 vs heatwaveR
text: Benchmarked Apple M3 Pro (12-core), macOS 15.5, R 4.5.3. speedup comes three sources: C++ algorithms. Climatology (sliding-window percentile) event detection (run-length encoding, gap joining, 19 metrics) implemented pure C++ rather R + data.table. OpenMP parallelism. pixel independent, OpenMP distributes pixels across cores zero coordination overhead. Direct NetCDF /O. Reads full data slab one C call via libnetcdf, avoiding R’s per-pixel ncdf4 random-access overhead.

code: library(parallel)  # Read the longitude coordinate once (cheap), to cut non-overlapping tiles. g <- heatwave3:::hw3_read_sst(   sst_file,   var_name,   time_range = c("1982-01-01", "1982-01-02") ) lon <- sort(unique(g$lon))  make_tiles <- function(n) {   pad <- 0.45 * min(diff(lon)) # < half the grid spacing   grp <- cut(seq_along(lon), breaks = n, labels = FALSE)   unname(lapply(split(lon, grp), function(L) c(min(L) - pad, max(L) + pad))) }  run_psock <- function(n_workers) {   cl <- makeCluster(n_workers, setup_strategy = "sequential")   on.exit(stopCluster(cl))   clusterEvalQ(cl, suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(heatwave3)))   clusterExport(cl, c("sst_file", "var_name", "clim_period"))   tiles <- make_tiles(n_workers)   parts <- parLapply(cl, tiles, function(lr) {     stem <- tempfile()     on.exit(unlink(paste0(stem, c("_clim.nc", "_events.nc"))))     out <- detect3(       sst_file,       name = stem,       climatologyPeriod = clim_period,       var_name = var_name,       lon_range = lr,       category = TRUE,       n_threads = 1L,  # 1 thread per worker!       quiet = TRUE     )     hw3_export(out[["events"]])   })   do.call(rbind, parts) }  system.time(evp <- run_psock(16L))

title: Detect spatially connected marine heatwave blobs — detect_blob3
text: function read pre-computed event file. Instead, takes raw SST data climatology, internally constructs 3D boolean exceedance mask comparing pixel's daily SST threshold climatology (temp > thresh heatwaves, temp < thresh cold-spells). Connected voxels 3D mask labelled coherent spatial events using union-find algorithm. approach used heatwaveR::detect_blob3(). reason event file detect_event3 used directly event file stores per-pixel event summaries (start/end dates, intensity metrics), daily per-pixel boolean mask needed spatial connectivity analysis.
